title: Training Notes: Late Document Renewals and Temporary License Acceptance on Wayfare Agreements
content:
These training notes cover a rule of the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product: a Wayfare driver's record of late renewals, across all documents, reduces the temporary license acceptance days, the calendar days from the upload day for which a paper temporary driver's license is accepted as the driver's license on file.

**Rule.** When the standing record holds five or more second expiry notices, for any document, dated fewer than 24 whole calendar months before the upload day, the temporary license acceptance days change by -10 days; when it holds three or four, they change by -6 days; when it holds one or two, they change by -3 days; when it holds none, they do not change.

| Second expiry notices, any document, dated fewer than 24 whole calendar months before the upload day | Change |
|---|---|
| 5 or more | -10 |
| 3 or 4 | -6 |
| 1 or 2 | -3 |
| none | 0 |

### Questions answered

**Does the document type matter?** No. Second expiry notices for the driver's license, the auto insurance, the vehicle inspection, the vehicle registration and the for-hire permit all count.

**Do first notices count?** No; only second expiry notices are counted.

**Which window?** A notice counts when it is dated fewer than 24 whole calendar months before the upload day.

**Hypothetical example.** Upload day 2026-08-10. Within the window the standing record holds second notices for the auto insurance (two), the vehicle inspection (one) and the vehicle registration (one), four in all: the change is -6.
